newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end lower, platinum sharply off.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end lower, platinum sharply off.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals ended lower Monday as options expired, with white metals sharply weaker, partly on talk that Russia would settle a debt by supplying platinum and palladium, traders said.
A continuing strong performance by the dollar against the mark and yen also discouraged investment in precious metals, Edward Kempf of CPM Group said.
COMEX June gold settled $2.50 weaker at $341.40 an ounce, traded $343.30 to $340.50. Bullion was quoted by dealers at $339.30/$339.80.
COMEX July silver ended 11.00 cents off at $4.658.
July silver was traded $4.75 to $4.63 an ounce.
Volume was relatively light in gold, at an estimated 17,000 lots, with silver at an estimated 25,000 lots.

"There was some fund selling in gold which was weighed down by the options expiry in London," a bullion trade source said. Over the counter options expired with the market straddling the key $340 per ounce strike price.
Early in the session in New York a fund also bought a large amount of options well below the market and sold futures against them, a move described by floor sources as a big bet on a downside move.
The dollar rallied overnight following the G7 meeting of industrialised nations to a 37-month high against the mark and near its 55-month peak against the yen.

"I think the whole of the precious metals complex has suffered in the hands of the strong dollar," Kempf said. Despite good physical demand for gold, money which had been invested in the greenback was also finding its way back into blue chip stocks, he added.

Meanwhile platinum and palladium were also dragged down to some extent by the weakness in gold and silver, but dealers said other factors also lay behind the weakness in white metals, despite a surge in palladium lease rates overnight.
Platinum and palladium had ended higher in Japan due to the weaker yen, and this allowed for the dollar price to come off a little, dealer sources said.

Also bearish for white metals was talk that Russia was paying a defaulted cash loan from Switzerland in platinum and palladium metal, swapping it for the $300 million of gold which it had put in the hands of the Swiss as collateral, a dealer said.
But there was still no firm dates given for shipments of Russian platinum and palladium to Japan.
July NYMEX platinum settled $5.20 off at $372.50 an ounce, traded $375.90 to $371.50.
June NYMEX palladium went out $2.90 weaker at $156.30 an ounce.
